newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL to invest HUF 400bln to 500bln by 2002.
newsitem.headline: MOL to invest HUF 400bln to 500bln by 2002.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL) plans to invest 400 billion to 500 billion forints over the next three to five years, MOL CEO Zoltan Mandoki told shareholders on Wednesday.
"We have to invest some 400 to 500 billion forints in the next three to five years," Mandoki said at the company's annual general meeting.

He added that MOL's main burden remained the state-controlled domestic gas sale price, which is causing the company's gas business to remain in the red despite legislation guaranteeing an eight percent return on equity for energy companies.
"The law is in force but I cannot say it is being applied," Mandoki said.
MOL imports at near market prices most of the gas it sells in Hungary at state-controlled prices.
This caused losses in its gas operations of 23.1 billion forints last year, compared to 13.1 billion forints in 1995 and 15.9 billion in 1994.
"The company cannot accept a policy that subsidises gas prices through a business venture," Mandoki said.

MOL hopes that the state will eventually make good its promise on pricing, he said, adding that the company will continue to expand its gas storage capacity as daily consumption during the winter peak is expected to rise to 100 million cubic meters from 76 million cubic meters during the winter of 1996/97.
Regarding foreign oil explorations, only the Tunisian one has proven successful recently, Mandoki said, but the company planned to continue its exploration in the Middle East.
Although MOL regards Russia as one of its main potential targets for exploration, the political, economic and legislative risks involved are too high, he added.
The company will continue streamlining this year with a 10 percent reduction of its workforce, after a similar reduction in 1996.
MOL also plans to trim its portfolio by selling its stake in some 30 companies out of more than 130 firms of which it is full or part owner, Mandoki said.

The rationalisation of MOL's refining and logistics resulted in savings of some 1.5 billion to two billion forints last year, but these savings are expected to rise to some 10 billion to 12 billion forints in 1998, a document prepared for the AGM said.
Shareholders approved a 37 forints per share or 3.7 percent dividend on the 1996 results, compared with 0.9 percent last year.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares closed at 3,380 forints, down 10.
